why: B moved the traffic that actually mattered and got it verified — the n=5 review ensemble ported off `n`, DeepSeek unlocked and mapped, every route confirmed (32/32 live) — while preserving behaviour where A gave it up, notably choosing claude-sonnet-4-6 at the same price because it still accepts temperature and keeping it via extra_body, rather than A's cheaper temperature:false target plus a silent loss of ideation diversity and reviewer determinism. A's system-level review is framed more sharply (who is waiting, what repeats, what fails) and its aider diagnosis and ICLR-bench-as-eval idea are the single best proposals in either report, but A also leaves the pipeline's largest prompt on OpenAI, wrongly calls DeepSeek routing an account decision rather than the code change B demonstrates, and has six unverified route sites.
A_best: The aider/LiteLLM investigation — pinning down why only the OpenAI provider honours litellm.client_session, proving the api_base route live (and that the dated id 404s), and ranking 'put the biggest spender on Router' #2 — plus shipping per-stage spend labels inside the migration so policy can key cache keys and models per stage, and proposing review_iclr_bench as the ground-truth harness for choosing the reviewer model.
B_best: Doing the unglamorous routing work instead of deferring it: porting the 5-way ensemble to per-call requests with honest cost math (+$0.10, roughly halved by the cache key), unlocking and mapping DeepSeek, keeping temperature via extra_body on a temperature-capable model, and i3's deterministic fixes that delete up to 9 of 10 full-context novelty rounds and stop two crashes from discarding a finished experiment and writeup.
A_worst: Mapping the default Claude path to claude-sonnet-5 (temperature:false) and then dropping temperature entirely — ideation's 0.75 and the reviewer's 0.1 silently gone, when B showed a one-line extra_body keeps them — compounded by declaring the DeepSeek/Gemini/OpenRouter paths an 'account decision, not a code change' (false for DeepSeek) and leaving the n=5 ensemble, the pipeline's largest prompt, on OpenAI.
B_worst: Leaving stage labels on an improvement branch, so the shipped migration's prompt_cache_key "$feature" and spend attribution collapse to one stack-derived label (the live data confirms 15 requests under ai_scientist/llm.py:get_response_from_llm) — and never interrogating latency/tier for a pipeline that is unattended end to end, nor diagnosing aider's Anthropic path as far as A did.
